subject: Infringement incident triage + Order Form liability allocation
messages:
From: Tom Garrett <tom.garrett@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Notice of alleged IP infringement (output from Redwood model)

Hi Marissa,

We discovered content in our product manuals that appears to be substantially similar to a portion of outputs generated by your hosted endpoint (example attached). We think this may be a third-party IP issue. Per the Order Form and MSA we have on file, we are providing notice and asking Redwood to confirm who will own defense/indemnity for any third-party claims arising from this output.

Key items:
- Alleged material: attached as "sample_output_and_source.pdf" inside the zip.
- Customer impact: our engineering team flagged two product pages that quote the output verbatim.
- Requested next steps: confirmation of receipt, request for evidence of source provenance, and a named contact for triage.

We appreciate a response within 48 hours due to potential release scheduling at Acme.

Best,
Tom Garrett
Head of Legal, Acme Robotics
Attachments: acme_allegation_package.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Garrett <tom.garrett@acme.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of alleged IP infringement (output from Redwood model)

Tom / Alyssa — thanks for the heads up, and we received the package.

Short answer: we will triage immediately. To set expectations:
- Initial acknowledgement (this email) within 2 hours (confirming receipt).
- Full technical provenance check and preliminary legal read within 48 business hours.
- We will identify an internal evidence owner who will coordinate deliverables back to you.

For coordination: Kimberly (cc'd) will lead the legal assessment of indemnity exposure and proposed allocation under the current Order Form. Ben will coordinate commercial outreach if there is a potential coverage/credit discussion.

Action items for Acme: please confirm whether Acme intends to preserve the product pages unchanged pending triage (release hold) and provide the timestamped artifacts you mentioned. That helps our forensic run.

We are attaching an empty evidence manifest template to collect what we'll need (will populate after our probe).

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
Attachment: evidence_manifest.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: triage plan, coverage matrix, and evidence owners (Acme notice)

Team — quick internal plan after initial review of Acme's packet. Summary and proposed approach below.

1) Immediate triage (Rishi) — engineering to snapshot model weights, prompt logs (where retained), and runtime provenance. Work with infra to preserve the request logs and KV caches for the relevant timeframe. Target: 24 hours.

2) Evidence owner mapping (Rishi + Marissa) — assign clear owners for: model provenance, customer artifacts, and legal chain-of-custody documents. See proposed mapping (Drive link above).

3) Coverage/Allocation matrix (Kim) — preliminary read of MSA + Order Form shows:
   - MSA broad indemnity clause covers third-party IP claims caused by Redwood's breach of obligations, but Order Form limits remedies and caps liability to order-specific fees.
   - Proposed triage outcome-driven allocation: if our provenance shows model output replicates an identifiable licensed corpus, offer defense with reservation + discuss limited reimbursement (credit) vs. full indemnity depending on severity and litigation posture.

4) Commercial escalation (Ben) — prepare a short commercial proposal (credit, escrow holdback, or joint notice flow) to offer if there's a non-litigation resolution.

5) Communications — recommended to externalize a single point of contact: Marissa for legal + Rishi for technical. Do not share internal kernel-level logs publicly; share redacted provenance report.

Please review and confirm owners. If we find evidence of third-party claim imminence (cease-and-desist filed), we'll escalate to leadership and recommend immediate defense-control vs. reimburse analysis.

-Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Garrett <tom.garrett@acme.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Notice of alleged IP infringement (output from Redwood model) — proposed approach and order form redline

Tom / Alyssa — thanks for your patience while we ran the initial internal checks. High-level findings and a proposed commercial/legal path below.

Preliminary findings (technical):
- Our short provenance run indicates the flagged model output matches a small set of examples from a third-party dataset used in pre-2020 training; we could not conclusively identify ingestion from Acme-sanctioned content.
- We have preserved request logs and a redacted provenance report is attached. (See evidence_manifest.pdf and forensic_summary.pdf in the Drive link.)

Proposed next steps and order form redline concept:
1) Defense/Indemnity: Redwood proposes to accept defense for third-party claims arising from our model outputs where (a) the claim relates to an identified third-party copyright that can be traced to our training set and (b) Redwood's internal review confirms no misuse of an Acme-supplied private corpus. We propose a mutual notice-and-cooperation flow and a shared evidence owner mapping.

2) Monetary exposure: because the Order Form caps aggregate liability, we propose the following allocation tiers in the redline (see attached docx):
   - Tier A (litigation filed): Redwood defends; reimbursement of reasonable settlement costs up to the Order Form cap; for amounts beyond cap, commercial credit or insurance offset discussion.
   - Tier B (non-litigation remediation): joint cooperative remediation; Redwood offers engineering credits up to X% of the last 12 months' spend.

3) Escrow / holdback: for high-risk releases, we propose a temporary release hold and short-term escrow of disputed funds pending root-cause analysis (documented procedure in the redline).

4) Evidence sharing: we will supply a redacted provenance report and a timeline of request/response pairs; we will not disclose kernel-level artifacts or unredacted training data.

Attached: orderform_proposed_redline.docx (track changes), evidence_manifest.pdf (populated), forensic_summary.pdf.

Requested from Acme: confirm whether Acme will accept the proposed two-week review window for the Tier A assessment and whether you will pause the release of the affected pages pending the review. Once we have your confirmation, we'll shift to a formal redline-and-exchange and route to procurement/legal on both sides.

If you'd like to discuss over a quick call, Ben can set up a 30-minute slot tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
Attachments: orderform_proposed_redline.docx, evidence_manifest.pdf, forensic_summary.pdf
